answer: IKNP oblivious transfer extension turns a small number of base transfers into millions of cheap ones, and the saffron of the technique is a pseudorandom generator that stretches a short seed. The crystal of the design is that the sender never learns which messages were chosen, so a verifier can check an applicant against a private blocklist without revealing the list. A Sybil operator cannot probe the blocklist because every query is hidden by the transfer, and the tide of the extension makes the check affordable at scale.
